marking_schemes.question_text: The salt solution which does not react with ammonium hydroxide is:
key_points: Calcium nitrate does not react with NH4OH
NH4OH forms precipitate with Pb2+, Zn2+, Cu2+, Fe2+, Fe3+ but not with Ca2+
common_errors: Choosing copper nitrate
Choosing lead nitrate
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates chose copper nitrate while others selected lead nitrate instead of calcium nitrate.

marking_schemes.question_text: The organic compound which undergoes substitution reaction is:
key_points: C2H6 is ethane, an alkane with general formula CnH2n+2
common_errors: Random choices indicating lack of knowledge that alkanes show substitution reactions
Not applying general formula to identify alkane
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates made random choices indicating they did not associate the fact that alkanes show substitution reactions or did not apply the general formula to select the correct alkane.

marking_schemes.question_text: The electrolysis of acidified water is an example of:
key_points: Electrolysis involves both oxidation at anode and reduction at cathode
Hence it is a redox reaction
common_errors: Writing only oxidation
Writing only reduction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates either wrote oxidation or reduction instead of redox reaction.

marking_schemes.question_text: The IUPAC name of dimethyl ether is:
common_errors: Giving varied incorrect names
Confusing with ethoxy methane
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates were unsure of the correct name and gave varied names.

marking_schemes.question_text: The catalyst used in the Contact Process is:
key_points: Contact process uses V2O5 as catalyst for oxidation of SO2 to SO3
common_errors: Choosing iron as catalyst
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates selected the correct option of vanadium pentoxide. However, a few chose iron which was incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one word or a phrase for the following statement: The energy released when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous isolated atom to form a negatively charged ion.
key_points: Electron affinity is the energy released when electron is added to neutral gaseous atom
common_errors: Writing electronegativity
Writing ionization potential
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instead of electron affinity, many candidates wrote electronegativity or ionization potential.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one word or a phrase for the following statement: Process of formation of ions from molecules which are not in ionic state.
key_points: Ionisation is the process of ion formation from neutral molecules
common_errors: Writing dissociation instead of ionization
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates wrote dissociation instead of ionization.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one word or a phrase for the following statement: The tendency of an element to form chains of identical atoms.
key_points: Catenation is the self-linking property of atoms to form chains
common_errors: Writing self-linking instead of catenation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote self-linking instead of Catenation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one word or a phrase for the following statement: The property by which certain hydrated salts, when left exposed to atmosphere, lose their water of crystallization and crumble into powder.
key_points: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallization on exposure to atmosphere
common_errors: Confusing efflorescence with deliquescence
Spelling errors
Writing effervescence
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates answered correctly. However, a few candidates got confused between efflorescence and deliquescence. Spelling errors were also noticed. Some referred to it as effervescence.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one word or a phrase for the following statement: The process by which sulphide ore is concentrated.
key_points: Froth floatation is used to concentrate sulphide ores
common_errors: Writing roasting
Writing calcination
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates wrote roasting or calcination instead of froth floatation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for each of the following: Action of concentrated sulphuric acid on carbon.
common_errors: Writing H2SO3 or H2CO3 as products
Leaving equation unbalanced
Writing Cu instead of C
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates erred by writing H2SO3 or H2CO3 among the products. Some left the equation unbalanced. A few wrote Cu instead of C.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for each of the following: Reaction of sodium hydroxide solution with iron (III) chloride solution.
common_errors: Using FeCl2 instead of FeCl3
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote the equation with FeCl2 instead of FeCl3.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for each of the following: Action of heat on aluminum hydroxide.
common_errors: Writing Al and H2O as products incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates incorrectly wrote the products as Al and H2O.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for each of the following: Reaction of zinc with potassium hydroxide solution.
common_errors: Writing incorrect formula of potassium zincate
Writing Zn(OH)2 or ZnO or K2O as products
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote incorrect formula of potassium zincate and many wrote one of the products as Zn(OH)2 or ZnO or K2O.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for each of the following: Action of dilute hydrochloric acid on magnesium sulphite.
common_errors: Confusing magnesium sulphite with sulphide or sulphate
Writing H2SO3 instead of H2O + SO2 as product
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates got confused between magnesium sulphite, sulphide and sulphate. Some others erred by writing H2SO3 instead of H2O + SO2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the IUPAC name for the following compound: H-C(=O)-H (structural formula showing H-C=O with H below C)
common_errors: Writing methanone instead of methanal
Confusing aldehyde suffix -al with ketone suffix -one
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote trivial or common names. Methanone was written instead of methanal.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the IUPAC name for the following compound: H-C-C-C-OH with H atoms on each carbon (propan-1-ol structural formula)
common_errors: Name ending in 'al' instead of 'ol'
Writing prop-1-ol incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Name ended by 'al' instead of 'ol' while some incorrectly wrote prop-l-ol.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the IUPAC name for the following compound: H3C-C(H)=C(H)-CH3 (but-2-ene structural formula)
common_errors: Writing 1,2-dimethylethene instead of but-2-ene
Writing simply butane or butan-2-ene
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: 1,2-dimethlyethene instead of 2-butene or but-2-ene. Some wrote simply butane or butan-2-ene.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write the structural formula of the two isomers of butane.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1. H-C-C-C-C-H (n-butane) OR CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3; 2. Branched isobutane OR H3C-CH(CH3)-CH3
key_points: Isobutane: branched chain with methyl group on C2
common_errors: Not understanding difference between straight and branched chains
Showing only carbon skeleton without hydrogen atoms
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates did not understand the difference between straight and branched chains clearly. Some showed the Carbon skeleton and missed showing the complete structural formula.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant observation for the following: Lead nitrate solution is treated with sodium hydroxide solution drop wise till it is in excess.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: White precipitate soluble in excess of sodium hydroxide solution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: White precipitate soluble in excess of sodium hydroxide solution.
key_points: White precipitate of Pb(OH)2 forms initially
Precipitate dissolves in excess NaOH to give colourless solution
marking_schemes.model_answer: A white precipitate is formed which dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide solution.
common_errors: Writing white Pb(OH)2 instead of white precipitate soluble
Writing insoluble in excess instead of soluble in excess
Writing white solution instead of colourless solution
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates wrote white Pb(OH)2 instead of white precipitate soluble. For solubility some wrote insoluble in excess or white solution instead of colourless solution.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant observation for the following: At the anode, when molten lead bromide is electrolyzed using graphite electrodes.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Reddish brown vapour at the anode.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Reddish brown vapour at the anode.
key_points: Bromine appears as reddish brown vapour/gas
marking_schemes.model_answer: Reddish brown vapour/gas is observed at the anode.
common_errors: Writing orange/red as colour of bromine
Forgetting to add the word vapour or gas
Writing that grey metal is deposited at anode
Writing equations instead of observations
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Colour of bromine was written as orange/red; some forgot to add the word vapour or gas; a few wrote that grey metal is deposited at the anode; several wrote equations instead of observations.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant observation for the following: Lead nitrate solution is mixed with dilute hydrochloric acid and heated.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: A white precipitate is formed which dissolves on heating or initially white precipitate is formed but on heating colourless solution is observed.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: A white precipitate is formed which dissolves on heating or initially white precipitate is formed but on heating colourless solution is observed.
key_points: PbCl2 dissolves on heating to give colourless solution
marking_schemes.model_answer: A white precipitate is formed initially which dissolves on heating to give a colourless solution.
common_errors: Writing reddish brown fumes of NO2 instead of white precipitate
Writing equation without stating colour of precipitate
Not mentioning effect of heating on solubility of PbCl2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instead of white precipitate many candidates wrote reddish brown fumes of NO2. Some wrote the equation without stating the colour of the precipitate. A few candidates expressed the answer by leaving out the effect of heating on the solubility of PbCl2.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant observation for the following: Anhydrous calcium chloride is exposed to air for some time.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Colourless solution or solid CaCl2 turns into solution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Colourless solution or solid CaCl2 turns into solution.
key_points: Absorbs moisture from air and turns into colourless solution
marking_schemes.model_answer: The solid anhydrous calcium chloride absorbs moisture from air and turns into a colourless solution.
common_errors: Writing that it turns hydrated
Writing that it turns powdery (confusion with efflorescent substances)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instead of writing that CaCl2 turns into colourless solution, candidates wrote that it turns hydrated. Some stated that it turns powdery having got confused with efflorescent substances.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one relevant observation for the following: Barium chloride solution is slowly added to sodium sulphate solution.
marking_schemes.model_answer: A white precipitate of barium sulphate is formed.
common_errors: Identifying product BaSO4 but missing word precipitate or colour white
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. However, a few candidates identified the product BaSO4 but missed out the word precipitate or the colour white.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Ionic compounds have a high melting point.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Oppositely charged ions are held by strong electrostatic force of attraction, so energy is required to separate them.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Oppositely charged ions are held by strong force of attraction or energy is required to separate the ions/ particles held by strong electrostatic force of attraction
key_points: Strong electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions
Large energy needed to overcome these forces
marking_schemes.model_answer: Oppositely charged ions in ionic compounds are held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction, requiring large amounts of energy to separate them, resulting in high melting points.
common_errors: Writing intermolecular force of attraction instead of strong electrostatic force of attraction between ions
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Intermolecular force of attraction instead of strong electrostatic force of attraction between ions was stated to be responsible for the high melting point.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Inert gases do not form ions.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Inert gases have stable electronic configuration or have 8 electrons in the valence shell / do not lose or gain electrons to form ions / complete outermost or valence shell.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Inert gases have stable electronic configuration or have 8 electrons in the valence shell (last shell) / do not lose or gain electrons to form ions/complete outermost or valence shell.
key_points: Inert gases have complete valence shell with 8 electrons (or 2 for helium)
No tendency to gain or lose electrons
marking_schemes.model_answer: Inert gases have a stable electronic configuration with 8 electrons in the valence shell (outermost shell is complete) and therefore do not lose or gain electrons to form ions.
common_errors: Writing that inert gases are stable without mentioning electronic configuration or 8 electrons in the valence shell
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote that inert gases are stable without mentioning electronic configuration or 8 electrons in the valence shell.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Ionisation potential increases across a period, from left to right.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Nuclear charge increases / nucleus exerts greater force of attraction on the valence electrons of same shell or atomic size decreases / the force of attraction on the valence electrons increases.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Nuclear charge increases / nucleus exerts greater force of attraction on the valence electrons of same shell or atomic size decreases / the force of attraction on the valence electrons are more i.e., increases.
key_points: Greater force of attraction on valence electrons
marking_schemes.model_answer: Across a period, nuclear charge increases while the number of shells remains the same, so the nucleus exerts greater force of attraction on the valence electrons. This means more energy is needed to remove a valence electron, hence ionisation potential increases.
common_errors: Not explaining the reason clearly
Not connecting nuclear charge increase to increased ionisation potential
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates could not explain the reason for increase in ionisation potential across a period, from left to right.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Alkali metals are good reducing agents.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Alkali metals have low ionization potential / have one electron in their valence shell and hence they easily lose or donate electron.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Alkali metals have low ionization potential / have one electron in their valence shell /and hence they easily lose or donate electron.
key_points: Alkali metals have one valence electron
Easily lose electron — act as reducing agents
marking_schemes.model_answer: Alkali metals have only one electron in their valence shell and have low ionisation potential, so they easily lose or donate this electron to other substances, acting as reducing agents.
common_errors: Not writing the correct reason relating to electron donation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates did not write the correct reason to explain alkali metals are good reducing agents.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Conductivity of dilute hydrochloric acid is greater than that of acetic acid.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Dilute hydrochloric acid undergoes complete ionization/dissociation whereas acetic acid undergoes incomplete or partial ionization / dilute HCl has higher concentration of ions than acetic acid / dilute HCl is a stronger acid than acetic acid / dilute HCl is a strong electrolyte and acetic acid is a weak electrolyte.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Dilute hydrochloric acid undergoes complete ionization/dissociation whereas acetic acid undergoes incomplete or partial ionization or dilute HCl has higher concentration of ions than acetic acid./Dilute hydrochloric acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid/strong electrolyte and acetic acid is a weak electrolyte/Dilute hydrochloric acid has higher degree of dissociation than acetic acid.
key_points: HCl is a strong acid — complete dissociation
Acetic acid is a weak acid — partial dissociation
HCl has higher concentration of ions
marking_schemes.model_answer: Dilute hydrochloric acid is a strong electrolyte that undergoes complete ionisation, producing a higher concentration of ions, whereas acetic acid is a weak electrolyte that undergoes only partial ionisation. Higher ion concentration results in greater conductivity.
common_errors: Writing about conductivity of each acid separately without comparing
Not relating conductivity to degree of ionisation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote about the conductivity of dilute HCl or acetic acid but could not compare the conductivity of both the acids.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the gas that is produced in the following case: Sulphur is oxidized by concentrated nitric acid.
key_points: Conc. HNO3 acts as oxidising agent producing NO2
common_errors: Writing SO2
Writing H2S
Writing N2
Writing both NO2 and SO2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instead of NO2 some candidates wrote SO2, H2S or N2 while some others wrote NO2 and SO2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the gas that is produced in the following case: Action of dilute hydrochloric acid on sodium sulphide.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most of the candidates answered this sub-part correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the gas that is produced in the following case: Action of cold and dilute nitric acid on copper.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Nitric oxide / nitrogen monoxide or NO
key_points: Cold dilute HNO3 reacts with copper to produce NO (nitric oxide)
common_errors: Calling it nitrogen oxide instead of nitric oxide
Writing NO2 instead of NO
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: While most candidates were able to give correct answer, but a few could not name the gas correctly, called it nitrogen oxide instead of nitric oxide or gave the incorrect answer NO2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the gas that is produced in the following case: At the anode during the electrolysis of acidified water.
key_points: Oxygen is produced at anode during electrolysis of acidified water
common_errors: Writing both hydrogen and oxygen, overlooking the specification of anode
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: While writing the name of the gas produced at the anode during the electrolysis of acidified water many candidates overlooked the term anode and wrote hydrogen and oxygen.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the gas that is produced in the following case: Reaction of ethanol and sodium.
common_errors: Writing ethane or ethene as the gas evolved
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates wrote ethane/ethene is evolved with the reaction of ethanol and sodium which was an incorrect answer.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill up the blank with the correct choice given in brackets: Ionic or electrovalent compounds do not conduct electricity in their _____________ state. (fused / solid)
key_points: Ionic compounds do not conduct in solid state as ions are not free to move
common_errors: Choosing fused
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates made errors in this subpart.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill up the blank with the correct choice given in brackets: Electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride solution will form _____________ at the cathode. (hydrogen gas / sodium metal)
key_points: H+ ions are preferentially discharged at cathode over Na+ ions
Hydrogen gas is produced at cathode
common_errors: Choosing sodium metal
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates made errors in this subpart.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill up the blank with the correct choice given in brackets: Dry hydrogen chloride gas can be collected by _____________ displacement of air. (downward / upward)
key_points: HCl gas is denser than air
Collected by upward displacement of air
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Attempted well by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill up the blank with the correct choice given in brackets: The most common ore of iron is _____________. (calamine / haematite)
key_points: Haematite (Fe2O3) is the most common ore of iron
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Attempted well by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: Fill up the blank with the correct choice given in brackets: The salt prepared by the method of direct combination is _____________. (iron (II) chloride / iron (III) chloride)
key_points: Iron (III) chloride is prepared by direct combination of iron and chlorine
common_errors: Choosing iron (II) chloride
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates made errors in this subpart.

marking_schemes.question_text: What do you understand by a lone pair of electrons?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: The pair of electrons which is not yet shared with other atoms in a covalent molecule is known as lone pair of electrons.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The pair of electrons which is not yet shared with other atoms in a covalent molecule is known as lone pair of electrons.
marking_schemes.model_answer: A lone pair of electrons is a pair of electrons in the valence shell of an atom that is not shared with any other atom in a covalent molecule.
common_errors: Missing key words: pair of electrons, not shared/unshared, or covalent molecule
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates could not define a lone pair of electrons completely. They missed out the key words in the definition like pair of electrons or not shared/unshared or covalent molecule.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the electron dot diagram of Hydronium ion. (H=1; O=8)
marking_schemes.correct_answer: H3O+ showing oxygen with one lone pair, three O-H bonds, and a positive charge, with coordinate bond indicated by arrow
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Electron dot diagram of H3O+ showing H-O-H with lone pair on O, positive charge, and coordinate bond arrow
key_points: Oxygen forms three bonds with hydrogen
Different symbols for O and H electrons
marking_schemes.model_answer: H3O+ with oxygen bonded to three H atoms, one lone pair on O, positive charge on ion, coordinate bond shown with arrow
common_errors: Missing lone pair
Missing positive charge
Using same kind of dots for electrons of both O and H
Not indicating coordinate bond by arrow
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The lone pair or the charge was missing; same kind of dots were used for electrons of both O and H; the coordinate bond was not indicated by an arrow.

marking_schemes.question_text: In Period 3 of the Periodic Table, element B is placed to the left of element A. The element B would have (lower / higher) metallic character than A.
key_points: Metallic character decreases from left to right across a period
B is to the left of A, so B has higher metallic character
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates attempted this question well barring a few exceptions.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: In Period 3 of the Periodic Table, element B is placed to the left of element A. The element A would probably have (lesser / higher) electron affinity than B.
key_points: Electron affinity increases from left to right across a period
A is to the right of B, so A has higher electron affinity
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates attempted this question well barring a few exceptions.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: In Period 3 of the Periodic Table, element B is placed to the left of element A. The element A would have (greater / smaller) atomic size than B.
key_points: Atomic size decreases from left to right across a period
A is to the right of B, so A has smaller atomic size
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates attempted this question well barring a few exceptions.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Copy and complete the following table which refers to the conversion of ions to neutral particles. Conversion: Chloride ion to chlorine molecule. Write the ionic equation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 2Cl1- – 2e → Cl2 or Cl- – e → Cl and Cl + Cl → Cl2 or 2Cl → Cl2
key_points: Two Cl- ions combine to form Cl2
accepted_alternatives: Cl- – e → Cl; Cl + Cl → Cl2
common_errors: Writing only Cl- + e- → Cl without forming Cl2
Incomplete equation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: In ionic equations such as Cl2 formation, equation Cl- + e- → Cl was given and the next equation was missed out.

marking_schemes.question_text: Copy and complete the following table which refers to the conversion of ions to neutral particles. Conversion: Chloride ion to chlorine molecule. State whether this is oxidation or reduction.
key_points: Cl- loses electrons to form Cl2
common_errors: Writing reduction instead of oxidation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The term oxidation/reduction was incorrectly associated with the ionic equations.

marking_schemes.question_text: Copy and complete the following table which refers to the conversion of ions to neutral particles. Conversion: Lead (II) ion to lead. Write the ionic equation.
common_errors: Writing Pb2+ – 2e → Pb (incorrect sign)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Pb2+ - 2e → Pb was a common error.

marking_schemes.question_text: Copy and complete the following table which refers to the conversion of ions to neutral particles. Conversion: Lead (II) ion to lead. State whether this is oxidation or reduction.
key_points: Pb2+ gains electrons to form Pb
common_errors: Writing oxidation instead of reduction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The term oxidation/reduction was incorrectly associated with the ionic equations.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write the balanced chemical equation to prepare ammonia gas in the laboratory by using an alkali.
common_errors: Using NaOH instead of Ca(OH)2
Using (NH4)2SO4 instead of NH4Cl
Writing NH4OH instead of NH3 as product
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some wrote methods using NaOH or using (NH4)2SO4 instead of NH4Cl. Some showed formation of NH4OH instead of NH3.

marking_schemes.question_text: State why concentrated sulphuric acid is not used for drying ammonia gas.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Concentrated sulphuric acid reacts with ammonia to form ammonium sulphate / NH3 being basic combines with concentrated H2SO4.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Concentrated sulphuric acid reacts with ammonia / form ammonium sulphate or NH3 being basic combines with concentrated H2SO4 / correct chemical equation.
key_points: Cannot be used for drying as it reacts with the gas
marking_schemes.model_answer: Concentrated sulphuric acid reacts with ammonia to form ammonium sulphate (2NH3 + H2SO4 → (NH4)2SO4), so it cannot be used for drying ammonia gas.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered this sub-part correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is ammonia gas not collected over water?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: NH3 is highly soluble in water / dissolves in water.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: NH3 is highly soluble in water or dissolves in water.
key_points: Ammonia is highly soluble in water
marking_schemes.model_answer: Ammonia is highly soluble in water and would dissolve in it rather than being collected.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered sub parts (ii) and (iii) of this question correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the acid used for the preparation of hydrogen chloride gas in the laboratory. Why is this particular acid preferred to other acids?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Concentrated sulphuric acid. It is nonvolatile / has high boiling point / displaces the volatile hydrogen chloride from the salt sodium chloride.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Concentrate sulphuric acid. It is nonvolatile / has high boiling point / displaces the volatile hydrogen chloride from the salt sodium chloride.
key_points: It is non-volatile/has high boiling point
It displaces volatile HCl from NaCl
marking_schemes.model_answer: Concentrated sulphuric acid is used. It is preferred because it is non-volatile and has a high boiling point, so it displaces the volatile hydrogen chloride gas from the sodium chloride salt without itself vaporizing.
common_errors: Not specifying concentrated
Writing that it does not react with HCl gas as the reason
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates did not specify whether sulphuric acid used should be concentrated or dilute. Some wrote that it does not react with HCl gas as the reason for preference.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write the balanced chemical equation for the laboratory preparation of hydrogen chloride gas.
common_errors: Not mentioning temperature condition below 200°C
Writing the equation for Na2SO4 formation at higher temperature
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates did not mention the necessary condition of temperature i.e., below 200°C to ensure Na2SO4 is not formed and ended up writing the incorrect equation.

marking_schemes.question_text: For the preparation of hydrochloric acid in the laboratory: Why is direct absorption of hydrogen chloride gas in water not feasible?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Back suction occurs / HCl gas dissolves in water at a faster rate than it is produced.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Back suction occurs (or the description of back suction) / HCl gas dissolves in water at a faster rate than it is produced.
key_points: HCl dissolves faster than it is produced
marking_schemes.model_answer: Direct absorption is not feasible because HCl gas is extremely soluble in water and dissolves faster than it is produced, causing water to rush back into the flask (back suction), which could crack the apparatus.
common_errors: Giving inadequate explanation without mentioning back suction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates gave inadequate explanation without mentioning the effect back suction.

marking_schemes.question_text: For the preparation of hydrochloric acid in the laboratory: What arrangement is done to dissolve hydrogen chloride gas in water?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Inverted funnel arrangement / the rim of the funnel just touches the surface of water taken in the trough.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Inverted funnel arrangement/ the rim of the funnel just touches the surface of water taken in the trough or correct diagram.
key_points: Rim of funnel just touches water surface
marking_schemes.model_answer: An inverted funnel arrangement is used where the rim of the funnel just touches the surface of water in the trough, preventing back suction.
common_errors: Writing thistle funnel instead of inverted funnel arrangement
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. However, a few candidates wrote thistle funnel instead of inverted funnel arrangement.

marking_schemes.question_text: For the electro-refining of copper: What is the cathode made up of?
key_points: Cathode is made of pure copper in electro-refining
common_errors: Writing impure copper
Just writing copper without specifying pure
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates missed out associating the word pure with it or wrote impure copper.

marking_schemes.question_text: For the electro-refining of copper: Write the reaction that takes place at the anode.
key_points: Cu loses 2 electrons to form Cu2+ ions
common_errors: Writing Cu + 2e- → Cu2+
Writing Cu2+ - 2e- → Cu (cathode reaction)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote incorrect reactions such as Cu + 2e- → Cu2+ or Cu2+ - 2e- → Cu.

marking_schemes.question_text: The percentage composition of a gas is: Nitrogen 82.35%, Hydrogen 17.64%. Find the empirical formula of the gas. [N = 14, H = 1]
key_points: Divide percentage by atomic mass to get number of atoms
Divide by smallest value to get ratio
common_errors: Dividing atomic weight by the individual percentage instead of percentage by atomic weight
Writing N3H as empirical formula
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates calculated the number of atoms by dividing atomic weight by the individual percentage. In the last step, some stated the empirical formula as N3H instead of NH3.

marking_schemes.question_text: Aluminum carbide reacts with water according to the following equation: Al4C3 + 12H2O → 4Al(OH)3 + 3CH4. What mass of aluminum hydroxide is formed from 12 g of aluminum carbide? [Relative molecular weight of Al4C3 = 144; Al(OH)3 = 78]
common_errors: Ignoring stoichiometric coefficients and not considering 4 moles of Al(OH)3
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates ignored the stoichiometric coefficients and did not consider 4 moles of Al(OH)3.

marking_schemes.question_text: Aluminum carbide reacts with water according to the following equation: Al4C3 + 12H2O → 4Al(OH)3 + 3CH4. What volume of methane at s.t.p. is obtained from 12 g of aluminum carbide? [Relative molecular weight of Al4C3 = 144]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 144 g Al4C3 → 3 x 22.4 L of CH4; Volume of CH4 = (3 x 22.4/144) x 12 = 5.6 L
key_points: 144 g Al4C3 gives 3 × 22.4 L of CH4
common_errors: Ignoring that 3 moles of CH4 are released per mole of Al4C3
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates ignored the fact that 3 moles of CH4 were released with every mole of Al4C3.

marking_schemes.question_text: If 150 cc of gas A contains X molecules, how many molecules of gas B will be present in 75 cc of B? The gases A and B are under the same conditions of temperature and pressure.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: No. of molecules of B = (75 × x)/150 = x/2
key_points: Equal volumes of gases at same T and P contain equal number of molecules
75 cc contains half the number in 150 cc
marking_schemes.model_answer: Number of molecules in 75 cc of B = (75/150) × X = X/2
common_errors: Writing 2X as the answer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. However, a few candidates wrote number of molecules of gas B as 2x instead of x/2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the law on which the above problem is based.
key_points: Avogadro's law: equal volumes of gases at same T and P contain equal number of molecules
common_errors: Naming the law as Gay Lussac's law
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates named the law as Gay Lussac's law which was incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the main component of the following alloy: Brass
key_points: Brass is an alloy mainly composed of copper (and zinc)
common_errors: Listing all components of brass instead of main component
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates listed all the components of the alloys instead of giving the main components as asked.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the main component of the following alloy: Duralumin
key_points: Duralumin is an alloy mainly composed of aluminum
common_errors: Listing all components of duralumin instead of main component
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates listed all the components instead of giving the main components as asked.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following table which relates to the homologous series of hydrocarbons. General formula CnH2n-2: Give the IUPAC name of the homologous series.
key_points: CnH2n-2 is the general formula for alkynes
common_errors: Writing name of compound instead of homologous series name
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Name of compound was written in place of homologous series.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following table which relates to the homologous series of hydrocarbons. General formula CnH2n-2: Give the characteristic bond type.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Triple covalent bond/ triple/≡ / C≡C/ CH≡CH
key_points: Alkynes have a triple covalent bond
common_errors: Writing unsaturated instead of triple covalent bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The characteristic bond was referred to as unsaturated/saturated instead of triple covalent bond.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following table which relates to the homologous series of hydrocarbons. General formula CnH2n-2: Give the IUPAC name of the first member of the series.
key_points: First member of alkynes is ethyne (C2H2)
Minimum 2 carbons needed to form a triple bond
common_errors: Writing methyne as first member of alkynes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The IUPAC name of the first member of the alkynes was given as methyne.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following table which relates to the homologous series of hydrocarbons. General formula CnH2n+2: Give the IUPAC name of the homologous series.
key_points: CnH2n+2 is the general formula for alkanes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates made errors in completing the table.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following table which relates to the homologous series of hydrocarbons. General formula CnH2n+2: Give the characteristic bond type.
common_errors: Writing saturated instead of single covalent bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The characteristic bond was referred to as saturated instead of single covalent bond.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following table which relates to the homologous series of hydrocarbons. General formula CnH2n+2: Give the IUPAC name of the first member of the series.
key_points: First member of alkanes is methane (CH4)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates made errors in completing the table.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the most common ore of the metal aluminum from which the metal is extracted. Write the chemical formula of the ore.
common_errors: Writing alumina or cryolite instead of Bauxite
Writing Al2O3.5H2O with incorrect number of water molecules
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote alumina or cryolite instead of Bauxite. Some gave chemical formula as Al2O3.5H2O where the number of water molecules was incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the process by which impure ore of aluminum gets purified by using concentrated solution of an alkali.
key_points: Baeyer's process uses concentrated NaOH to purify bauxite
common_errors: Writing Hall's process
Writing Hoope's Process
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates named the process as Hall's process or Hoope's Process in place of Baeyer's process.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write the equation for the formation of aluminum at the cathode during the electrolysis of alumina.
key_points: Al3+ ions gain 3 electrons at cathode
common_errors: Writing Al – 3e- → Al3+
Writing Al + 3e- → Al3+
Writing 2Al3+ + 6e- → Al (incorrect balancing)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few got confused and wrote equations like Al – 3e- → Al3+ or Al + 3e- → Al3+ or 2Al3+ + 6e- → Al.

marking_schemes.question_text: A compound X (having vinegar like smell) when treated with ethanol in the presence of the acid Z, gives a compound Y which has a fruity smell. The reaction is: C2H5OH + X →(Z) Y + H2O. Identify Y and Z.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Y: Ethyl acetate / Ethyl ethanoate / CH3COOC2H5; Z: Concentrated H2SO4
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Y: Ethyl acetate / Ethyl ethanoate / CH3COOC2H5; Z: Concentrated H2SO4
key_points: Y is ethyl acetate/ethyl ethanoate (fruity smell)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Y: Ethyl acetate (ethyl ethanoate, CH3COOC2H5); Z: Concentrated sulphuric acid (H2SO4)
common_errors: Identifying Y as C2H5COOCH3
Just writing ester without specific name
Not mentioning concentrated for acid Z
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates identified compound Y as C2H5COOCH3 while some identified it as ester. A few candidates did not mention the strength of the acid.

marking_schemes.question_text: A compound X (having vinegar like smell) when treated with ethanol in the presence of the acid Z, gives a compound Y which has a fruity smell. Write the structural formula of X.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Structural formula of acetic acid: H-C(H)(H)-C(=O)-OH
key_points: Structural formula shows CH3 group and COOH group
common_errors: Drawing incorrect structure of acetic acid
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates drew an incorrect structure of compound X.

marking_schemes.question_text: A compound X (having vinegar like smell) when treated with ethanol in the presence of the acid Z, gives a compound Y which has a fruity smell. Name the above reaction.
key_points: Reaction between alcohol and acid to form ester is esterification
common_errors: Calling it catalysis
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of candidates named the reaction correctly. However, a few called it catalysis which was not correct.

marking_schemes.question_text: Ethane burns in oxygen to form CO2 and H2O according to the equation: 2C2H6 + 7O2 → 4CO2 + 6H2O. If 1250 cc of oxygen is burnt with 300 cc of ethane. Calculate the volume of CO2 formed.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Volume of CO2 formed = (4/2) x 300 = 600 cc
marking_schemes.model_answer: From the equation, 2 volumes C2H6 produce 4 volumes CO2. So 300 cc C2H6 produces (4/2) × 300 = 600 cc CO2.
common_errors: Using volume of O2 to calculate volume of CO2
Copying volume of ethane incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates incorrectly used volume of O2 to calculate the volume of CO2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Ethane burns in oxygen to form CO2 and H2O according to the equation: 2C2H6 + 7O2 → 4CO2 + 6H2O. If 1250 cc of oxygen is burnt with 300 cc of ethane. Calculate the volume of unused O2.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Volume of O2 used = (7/2) x 300 = 1050 cc; Volume of unused oxygen = 1250 – 1050 = 200 cc
common_errors: Not calculating volume of unused O2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates did not calculate the volume of unused O2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Three solutions P, Q and R have pH value of 3.5, 5.2 and 12.2 respectively. Which one of these is a weak acid?
key_points: Weak acid has pH closer to 7 but below 7
marking_schemes.model_answer: Solution Q (pH 5.2) is a weak acid.
common_errors: Writing solution P (pH 3.5) as the weak acid
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote solution P having value of pH 3.5 as that of a weak acid.

marking_schemes.question_text: Three solutions P, Q and R have pH value of 3.5, 5.2 and 12.2 respectively. Which one of these is a strong alkali?
marking_schemes.model_answer: Solution R (pH 12.2) is a strong alkali.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a chemical test to distinguish between the following pairs of chemicals: Lead nitrate solution and Zinc nitrate solution.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: By adding ammonium hydroxide in excess. Lead nitrate solution gives a white precipitate while Zinc Nitrate solution gives a colourless solution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: By adding ammonium hydroxide in excess. Lead nitrate solution gives a white precipitate while Zinc Nitrate solution gives a colourless solution.
key_points: Pb(NO3)2 gives white precipitate insoluble in excess NH4OH
Zn(NO3)2 gives white precipitate soluble in excess NH4OH to give colourless solution
marking_schemes.model_answer: Add ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH) in excess to both solutions. Lead nitrate gives a white precipitate that is insoluble in excess NH4OH, while zinc nitrate gives a white precipitate that dissolves in excess NH4OH to give a colourless solution.
common_errors: Giving dry heating test for solutions
Using NaOH instead of NH4OH
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates ignored the solution state and gave dry heating test. Some candidates used NaOH in place of NH4OH.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a chemical test to distinguish between the following pairs of chemicals: Sodium chloride solution and Sodium nitrate solution.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: By adding silver nitrate / lead nitrate solution. Sodium chloride gives a white precipitate while sodium nitrate gives no precipitate / colourless solution / remains unchanged.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: By adding silver nitrate / lead nitrate solution. Sodium chloride gives a white precipitate while sodium nitrate gives no precipitate / colourless solution / remains unchanged. (alternate correct chemical test accepted)
key_points: NaCl gives white precipitate of AgCl or PbCl2
marking_schemes.model_answer: Add silver nitrate solution to both. Sodium chloride gives a white precipitate of silver chloride (AgCl), while sodium nitrate gives no precipitate and the solution remains unchanged.
accepted_alternatives: Using lead nitrate solution as the reagent
common_errors: Using concentrated H2SO4 to distinguish, overlooking both are in solution form
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates used concentrated H2SO4 to distinguish between NaCl and NaNO3 overlooking the fact that both were in solution form.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced equation for the preparation of the following salt: Copper sulphate from Copper carbonate.
common_errors: Using Na2SO4 solution instead of H2SO4
Writing two equations using HCl and H2SO4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instead of reaction with H2SO4, a few candidates used Na2SO4 solution.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced equation for the preparation of the following salt: Zinc carbonate from Zinc sulphate.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: ZnSO4 + Na2CO3 → ZnCO3 + Na2SO4 OR ZnSO4 + (NH4)2CO3 → (NH4)2SO4 + ZnCO3
key_points: Use soluble carbonate like Na2CO3 or (NH4)2CO3
common_errors: Using H2CO3 solution instead of Na2CO3
Two-step approach via ZnCl2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instead of Na2CO3 solution, a few candidates used H2CO3 solution. Some used two steps to obtain ZnCO3.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the type of salt formed when the reactants are heated at a suitable temperature for the preparation of Nitric acid?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Acid salt / bisulphate / hydrogen sulphate / NaHSO4 / KHSO4
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Acid Salt/ bisulphate/ hydrogen sulphate/ NaHSO4/ KHSO4
key_points: NaNO3 + H2SO4 → NaHSO4 + HNO3 at moderate temperature
marking_schemes.model_answer: Acid salt (bisulphate / hydrogen sulphate, e.g. NaHSO4)
common_errors: Writing normal salt instead of acid salt
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instead of acid salt, some candidates wrote normal salt.

marking_schemes.question_text: State why for the preparation of Nitric acid, the complete apparatus is made up of glass.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: The vapour of nitric acid being highly corrosive / HNO3 vapours attack rubber, cork etc. / HNO3 vapours do not react with glass.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The vapour of nitric acid being highly corrosive/ HNO3 vapours attack rubber, cork etc./ HNO3 vapours do not react with glass.
marking_schemes.model_answer: The vapours of nitric acid are highly corrosive and attack rubber and cork. Glass is used because HNO3 vapours do not react with glass.
common_errors: Stating that rubber will melt due to heat or cork will break
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly but a few stated that rubber will melt due to heat or cork will break.

marking_schemes.question_text: Which property of sulphuric acid is shown by the reaction of concentrated sulphuric acid with: Ethanol?
key_points: Conc. H2SO4 removes water from ethanol
common_errors: Writing drying instead of dehydration
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates wrote drying instead of dehydration.

marking_schemes.question_text: Which property of sulphuric acid is shown by the reaction of concentrated sulphuric acid with: Carbon?
key_points: Conc. H2SO4 oxidizes carbon to CO2
common_errors: Writing acidic property instead of oxidising property
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates stated acidic property instead of oxidising property.
